acceptance: The record cites the original decision (the Explorer build contract's removed_legacy list and the results platform strategy document), states its purpose, and says whether that purpose is affected by a file generated from results.duckdb.

Each option is assessed against the single-source rule, maintenance cost, and what a fetch-only client and a scripted client can each do today, with the measured size and fetch behaviour of the current artifacts.
The record uses the evidence gate's observations of whether any probe session tried to fetch a results index, results.duckdb or a bundle.
The owner's choice is recorded in the document. If the choice is (b) or (c), the record names the follow-up item for the owner to file; this item creates no build work itself.
The record is placed with the existing decision records and linked from the strategy document.
context:
Origin: adversarial review on 2026-11-13 of work first left unfiled. The earlier reasons assumed a person at the keyboard; this item records the corrected disposition. Line numbers are hints; re-read the cited file before relying on them.

Evidence (2026-11-13): results.duckdb is served with content length 14,168,064; a single bundle JSON is about 23 KB and returns 200; the strategy document's rule rejects any metric-looking key in manifest.json and prefers deriving all navigation from DuckDB.

Decision gate: this whole item is the gate. Do not start generator work under it. If the static result pages already let a client enumerate results, say so and recommend (a).

Verification rubric: pass only if the owner's decision is written into the record and each option has its evidence.

Guardrails: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. One PR per item, squash-merged to develop (site work: one PR in BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site). Add a changelog.d fragment for any user-facing change. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers) runs only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy (make comment-policy-check). Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review must be re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.
description:
Problem: the Explorer migration removed the JSON index files (manifest.json, benchmarks/, details/, compare/, meta_leaderboard.json) so that the browser pages had one source of metric truth, results.duckdb. That decision considered the browser client only. results.duckdb is a 14 MB binary: a client that can only fetch text cannot read it, and a script needs DuckDB and knowledge of the schema. Nothing lets a program list result IDs by benchmark, scale and platform except parsing the HTML summaries.

Outcome: a decision record that states whether the earlier removal applies to non-browser readers and chooses one option: (a) nothing more, the static result and summary pages are enough; (b) a small index generated from results.duckdb at build time with a parity check; (c) a tabular export such as Parquet or CSV.

This item delivers the decision record only. It changes no generator, contract or site code.
drop_reason: Dropped by owner decision on 2026-11-13: no reader has asked for an index, and bundle JSON and results.duckdb already return 200. No successor.
